transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-09-18 16:30 UTC | Duration: 52 mins | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM); Priya (Avalon Head of ML), Ethan (Platform), Renee (Security), Marco (SRE)

Auto summary (auto-generated): Quick discovery on cost levers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private. Focus on per-token pricing, batching & caching strategies, routing options, and security/compliance for an enterprise pilot. Agreed to run bench and share pricing plus SOC2 docs.

Topics: cost/unit economics, batching and KV cache, quantization tradeoffs, routing (region vs cost), Dedicated sizing, VPC/private constraints, timeline for pilot

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call so I know who we have.
[00:05] Priya (Avalon): Hi I'm Priya, head of ML at Avalon. We own the model infra decisions and cost for the product team.
[00:08] Ethan (Avalon): Ethan here, platform eng, I manage our k8s clusters and cost tracking.
[00:11] Renee (Avalon Sec): Renee, security. I'll focus on compliance and data flow.
[00:14] Sofia: Great. Daniel, want to intro?
[00:15] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yeah, hi all. Daniel, infra and serving. Today we'll walk through cost levers and deployment modes — hosted API baseline, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs.
[00:30] Priya: Our immediate ask: we have an aggressive budget for Q4 and need to understand if we should start on Hosted and move to Dedicated or start with Private. Mostly driven by token costs and P95 latency.
[00:40] Daniel: Makes sense. Quick question: what are your rough volumes and average request sizes?
[00:45] Priya: We're at about 1.2M tokens per day currently, average payload ~1.2k tokens/req, peak batching patterns around morning spikes. Target is up to 5M/day in 3 months.
[00:55] Marco (Avalon SRE): Also we need <250ms p95 for short completions (under 256 tokens) and endpoint routing across eu-west and us-east.
[01:05] Daniel: Ok that profile actually benefits from caching and batching levers. For Hosted per-token pricing we typically show a baseline rate for the model family — that covers CPU/kv cache overhead — then you can reduce unit cost with batching and prefix KV caching.
[01:20] Ethan: When you say KV caching, you mean the key-value attention cache for hot prefixes? Does that survive across requests?
[01:27] Daniel: Good question. Yes, Redwood's prefix/KV cache persists hot contexts for a short TTL per customer, so repeated prompts or system messages avoid recomputation. It can cut egress token compute by 20-60% depending on repetition. Sometimes transcript shows it as 'KV cash' in older notes ha.
[01:40] Priya: That variance is big. We have many templated prompts so caching could help. But what about batching? Our latency sensitivity worries me — batching increases throughput but can add tail latency.
[01:50] Daniel: Right — continuous batching is workload-aware. You can set latency SLOs and trade batch size/timeouts. For example with 50ms batching window you might see 2-3x throughput improvement with only ~20ms median added. If you need strict p95 under 250ms we can set smaller window or route critical paths to a low-latency tier.
[02:10] Sofia: Important distinction: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and simple per-token billing. Dedicated gives lower per-token but requires reserved GPU commitment. Private has similar economics to Dedicated once you add infra costs, but gives total control for compliance.
[02:25] Renee: For Private we need to confirm KMS key management, audit logs, and whether telemetry leaves the VPC. Also encryption in transit and at rest — and SOC2 evidence.
[02:35] Sofia: We will share SOC2 and the VPC runbook. For Private, telemetry can be configured to stay in customer network and you control KMS — Redwood can support BYOK HSM.
[02:45] Priya: Pricing — can you give a concrete worked example? Say 5M tokens/month with our profile (avg 1.2k tokens/req).
[02:55] Daniel: Sure. Hosted example: model X is $0.0008 per token for input + $0.0012 per output token as a combined effective rate — rough numbers. With batching and cache you might reduce effective unit cost by 35% to ~$0.0013 per token. That yields about $6.5k/mo for 5M tokens.
[03:15] Priya: Wait, that seems low for output-inclusive. Are those numbers per 1k tokens? I think earlier notes had per-K tokens in other vendors.
[03:23] Sofia: Good catch — sorry, these are per-token in decimal form; we usually quote per 1k tokens in the price sheet. We'll send the sheet with per-1k breakdown. Example: that's ~$1.30 per 1k tokens after batching/caching applied.
[03:37] Marco: If we did Dedicated, what's the economics?
[03:40] Daniel: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools. For your profile we recommend starting with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (or 8x for redundancy/throughput). Committed monthly price converts to effective per-token with utilization. If you run at 60-70% utilization, your unit cost can drop 30-50% from Hosted — depends on batching, q configs.
[04:00] Ethan: How do quantization options fit? We have some concerns about slightly lower quality if we quantize aggressively.
[04:06] Daniel: Right — quantization (8-bit, 4-bit) reduces memory and can increase throughput. Redwood gives model-quality profiles per quant setting. Typically 8-bit has negligible quality impact for many tasks; 4-bit sometimes needs eval. We recommend running A/B evals as part of the pilot.
[04:22] Priya: So for our use-case (few-shot summarization), 4-bit might be okay but we need evals.
[04:28] Daniel: Exactly. We'll include quantization recommendations for your prompt set.
[04:32] Renee: Back to security: if you go Hosted, does Redwood retain prompts? What about retention windows and ability to opt-out?
[04:38] Sofia: Hosted retains telemetry for X days by default for debugging, but you can opt into stricter retention or disable data retention for an enterprise plan. Dedicated and Private give you more control; Private means data never leaves your network unless you opt into metrics sharing.
[04:55] Priya: Timeline constraint: legal wants a 30-day pilot agreement; product wants to ship a feature mid-Q4. So 2-3 week pilot preferred.
[05:05] Sofia: We can propose a 2-week Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity and routing rules. If you like the ease, you can then either keep Dedicated or move to Private for compliance.
[05:14] Ethan: For routing, can we route critical requests to Dedicated and background to Hosted to save cost?
[05:18] Daniel: Yes — Redwood supports routing policies: by route, latency tier, or percentage. You can set fallbacks, so if Dedicated is saturated it can spill to Hosted. This gives a safety net for bursty traffic.
[05:30] Marco: What about cross-region perf? We need eu-west and us-east. If Dedicated sits in a single region, the cross-region latency sucks.
[05:36] Daniel: You can deploy Dedicated in multiple regions or use geo routing. For cost reasons teams often put Dedicated in primary region and use Hosted fallback in other regions; depends on SLOs.
[05:50] Priya: Can you share a sample invoice for the Hosted route vs Dedicated amortization so our finance team sees delta?
[05:56] Sofia: Yes we'll send the pricing sheet and a pro-forma invoice showing amortized per-token cost at various utilization points.
[06:05] [crosstalk] Lena (Redwood CSM): We'll also include example billing for burst credits.
[06:10] Priya: Are there any gotchas on the Dedicated autoscaling — like cold-starts when adding GPU nodes?
[06:16] Daniel: Autoscaling for Dedicated can be configured with warm pools and pre-warmed images to reduce cold-starts. Worst-case scale-up is a few mins but we can supply reserved burst capacity for spikes.
[06:30] Ethan: On measurement — how do we measure effective unit cost post-batching? We need token-level attribution in our billing.
[06:38] Sofia: Redwood Console provides token-level and route-level breakdowns, per-token cost by model and quantization config, and trace links to requests. We'll give you demo access for pilot.
[06:48] Marco: Any competitor comparison notes? We currently compare with running models on our own infra vs Anthropic/OpanAI for hosted.
[06:54] Daniel: For customers who have heavy steady load, self-hosting can be cheaper but comes with ops overhead. Compared to other hosted vendors, Redwood optimizes kernels and batching for inference which usually yields better cost per token under production workloads.
[07:10] Priya: Ok let's talk specific numbers for the pilot. Our expected pilot load is 50 req/sec with avg 1.2k token/req during peak, about 3M tokens over 2 weeks.
[07:22] Daniel: For a 2-week Dedicated pilot we'd size 4 GPUs with burst pool. We can produce a forecast: per-token effective cost at 65% util and with 30% batching improvement.
[07:34] Sofia: We'll include 3 scenarios in the deck: Hosted-only, Dedicated pilot (4 GPUs), and Private (customer VPC) with infra cost estimate.
[07:45] Renee: Also share the redaction/PII guidance: we need support for in-flight redaction or redact-at-rest options.
[07:52] Daniel: We have pre-processing hooks and field-level redaction. For Private you can do everything in-network. For Hosted/Dedicated we support tokenization-level redaction and configurable retention.
[08:05] Priya: One more operational question — can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[08:09] Daniel: Yes. Redwood supports model version pinning, canaries, A/B, and automatic fallbacks to older model variants if the new one regresses. The Console will show regressions against your eval set.
[08:20] Sofia: Anything else from legal side?
[08:22] Renee: We'll need the DPA, SCCs (if needed), and a SOC2 report. Also a contact for any pen-test coordination.
[08:30] Sofia: We'll send legal contacts and the docs.
[08:33] Priya: Great. On acceptance criteria for pilot: cost per 1k tokens under $1.1 post-batching, p95 latency under 250ms for short jobs, and no data leaving our VPC in Private option.
[08:45] Sofia: Noted. We'll map those to the pilot deliverables.
[08:50] Daniel: I'll scope the benchmark and we can use your prompt set. For quantization, we'll test 8-bit vs 4-bit and measure quality delta on your eval set.
[08:59] Priya: Timeline — legal review and NDA first then pilot next week, ideally start 2026-09-28.
[09:05] Sofia: We'll get the NDA and pricing to you by EOD tomorrow and lock the benchmark window.
[09:10] Ethan: For the bench, what telemetry do you need from our side?
[09:13] Daniel: Sample prompt set, request distribution (tokens per request, concurrency), and an S3 or artifact with labels for evals. Also network egress constraints if any.
[09:25] Marco: We'll provide a short runbook on network/firewall rules for Dedicated and the VPC peering steps.
[09:30] Priya: Final question — if Dedicated is saturated and spills to Hosted, how does billing work? We prefer predictable billing.
[09:36] Sofia: Billing is straightforward: Dedicated monthly commitment + usage overage billed at a negotiated overage rate; Hosted traffic billed at Hosted per-token rates. We can include a buffer in the pilot contract so you don't get surprises.
[09:50] Priya: Ok that's helpful.
[10:00] Sofia: Quick recap and next steps: 1) Redwood sends pricing + SOC2 + DPA; 2) Avalon shares prompt set and SLOs; 3) Redwood proposes Dedicated pilot plan and scheduling; 4) Legal signs NDA to unblock pilot.
[10:18] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:22] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up with an email summarizing next steps.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript includes some auto-transcription errors in names and technical terms (e.g., "KV cash"), occasional filler words. Conversation emphasized concrete pricing examples, pilot scope, quantization evals, routing and fallback, and compliance needs.
